parsed.corrected_rationale: The answer raises a concrete, paper-specific limitation scenario: GWDS may not significantly improve throughput and adversarial robustness if a mobile CNN already adopts DWS or similar techniques. It does not, however, point to a specific section, table, or figure of the paper, so the authors cannot confidently determine which part the comment addresses, even though it touches on identifiable unique aspects of the paper (GWDS, DWS, mobile CNN throughput and adversarial robustness). In terms of specificity, the comment clearly states what the issue is — the limitation that GWDS fails to deliver gains when DWS-like techniques are already used — so it is not highly unspecific; it is only unspecific about which part of the paper it refers to. Under the rubric, a comment whose referenced part cannot be confidently pinpointed but which clearly specifies what needs to be addressed falls in the middle of the scale, so it does not qualify as not grounded at all.
